review.summary:
Phase 91's source gate is substantiated by verified, source-bound evidence rather than prose. The phase-90 blocking defect is genuinely fixed: `crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:766-776` now charges the property-key copy budget before suppressing an omitted default, and `crates/scm-sdk/tests/schema_contracts.rs:45-87` proves both limit outcomes flip at the identical boundary (copied 26..=70 crossing at 42; work and node bounds 1..=64 compared for equal acceptance and equal error kind). Acceptance parity is not asserted, it is measured: `crates/scm-sdk/tests/schema_contracts.rs:252-285` replays the whole independent Zod oracle corpus (60,271 JSON cases, confirmed by the recorded `schema-oracle.mts --check` output at docs/checks/phase-91.json:616) under `Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults`, asserting identical accept/reject outcomes and that every differing key was absent from the input. The design makes this structural: `walk()` never branches on the new mode, so only `object()` and `parse_optional_with_limits` suppress output, and union/one-of selection depends solely on Ok/Err.

Scope coverage matches the plan. `crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_resources_contracts.rs:2027-2154` exercises all seven target entry points, asserts exact serialized equality with the server document (`same()` at line 144), covers explicit nulls and nested nulls, two distinct `list_all` pages with asserted `skip`/`limit` query pairs, original operation names (`red_team.targets.*`), and invalid-document rejection under both policies. Propagation through buffered alternative contracts and Gateway SSE is proven at `crates/scm-sdk/src/engine/tests.rs:2461-2533`; `operation_options` clones caller options so the flag survives paging. Request validation is untouched (`crates/scm-sdk/src/engine.rs:538` hardcodes `Mode::Request`), and all sampled defaulted fields are `Optional` with serde defaults, so suppression cannot break typed decoding.

The 49-command gate in docs/checks/phase-91.json matches `tools/check_phase.py:81-129` exactly, every command exits 0, `source_unchanged` is true, and the recorded SHA256 equals the reviewed source. Evidence is real, not asserted: both compilers run packaged archives that execute the new offline example (docs/checks/phase-91-package-1.89.0.json:778-796), the package delta against the published 0.1.0 archive is enumerated and allowlisted (`scripts/verify-publication.py:169-175`), dependencies are freshly scanned, the 100-process tracing stress runs at the explicitly reviewed 203-test count, and the private-material scan is bound to the reviewed source. The live refresh was re-executed after runtime edits, is version-bound (`tools/live_evidence.py:266,276`), and its failures (three 403s, two unexplained 400s, one uncorrelated scan-ID lookup) are recorded honestly, including the failed attempt-07 parser run. The 23-binding inventory is generated from frozen sources, reproducible, and distinguishes shared bindings by source node identity.

The deductions are documentation- and guardrail-shaped, not functional. README.md:18-19 states that a crates.io 0.1.1 release and docs.rs documentation "correspond to this version," and three documents link a publication receipt that does not exist — and the very test that used to enforce publication/document consistency now skips because the version changed. Nothing in the gate catches this. The remaining findings are small governance gaps: the committed-range whitespace check that phase 90 carried was dropped, the sidecar's three Rust API names are an unbound literal, the changelog omits the newly packaged example, and phase-status bookkeeping lags the passing gate. None is a blocker; all are locally fixable before the commit/push step.

findings.description: README states as present fact that "The [registry release](https://crates.io/crates/scm-sdk/0.1.1) and [API documentation](https://docs.rs/scm-sdk/0.1.1/scm_sdk/) correspond to this version", and lines 20-21 link docs/checks/release-registry-0.1.1.json. That receipt does not exist (only release-registry-0.1.0.json is present), crates.io has no 0.1.1, and docs/phase-status.json:2176 correctly records delivery as "not_yet_published". The plan's command sequence commits and pushes this source to main before `cargo publish` runs, so the authorized remote would carry an unverified publication claim. docs/RELEASE.md:6-8 and docs/STABILITY.md:3-5 get this right by hedging with "retained after actual upload"; README is the inconsistent outlier. Nothing in the 49-command gate guards the claim, because the test that enforced publication/document consistency now skips (see the separate finding).
findings.required_fix: Reword README.md:18-21 to match the hedged phrasing already used in docs/RELEASE.md:6-8 and docs/STABILITY.md:3-5 (state the crate version and that the registry release, docs.rs page and receipt are recorded after actual upload), and either defer the active crates.io/docs.rs/receipt links to the step-8 evidence-only commit or add an assertion in tools/test_g10_release.py::test_current_version_statements_are_bound_independently_of_publication that the unconditional "registry release ... correspond" phrasing and the release-registry-<version>.json link appear only when that receipt file exists and records the same version.

findings.description: test_verified_publication_is_consistent_in_current_release_documents calls self.skipTest() as soon as the workspace version differs from the recorded publication, which is now permanently true for 0.1.1 (confirmed skipped in docs/checks/phase-91.json:244). Everything after line 219 therefore no longer runs for any version: the obsolete-prose regex over README.md, CHANGELOG.md and every docs/*.md (lines 222-229), the "crates.io" presence check for CHANGELOG/STABILITY/SECURITY (lines 230-231), and the changelog-versus-receipt cross-check (lines 232-234). The replacement tools/test_g10_release.py:59-66 only compares version strings. The repository thus lost its publication/document consistency guard at exactly the release where an unverified publication claim was introduced.
findings.required_fix: Split the version-independent half of the test out of the skip: run the obsolete-prose regex and the crates.io-presence assertions unconditionally, and keep only the receipt-dependent comparisons (lines 220-221, 232-234) behind the version guard. Alternatively replicate the version-independent assertions in tools/test_g10_release.py so every gate run exercises them.

findings.description: The phase-91 command list begins with only `git diff --check` and `git diff --cached --check`. Phase 90's list (tools/check_phase.py:73) additionally ran `git diff --check 840c090..HEAD`, which was the explicit resolution of phase-90 review findings (docs/phase-status.json:1890-1898 and 1945-1953: "Replace the fixed a6d63e5 range end with actual HEAD, so later committed governance changes remain inside the whitespace check"). Because HEAD is now cc744c8 and the G10 changes are staged against it, the content committed in cc744c8 is covered by neither the working-tree nor the cached check, so a phase-90 fix is effectively reverted for the phase-91 gate.
findings.required_fix: Add ["git", "diff", "--check", "840c090..HEAD"] to the phase-91 command list in tools/check_phase.py:82-84 so committed maintenance-track changes stay inside the whitespace check, and rerun the gate.

findings.description: rustOnlyAdditions is a hardcoded Python literal copied into contracts/response-defaults.json:12-16, with no binding to the Rust source. tools/test_g10_release.py:39 asserts only `len(expected["rustOnlyAdditions"]) == 3`. docs/g10-0.1.1-plan.md:118-120 requires the sidecar be "checked against frozen sources and executable Rust tests"; the 23 bindings are so bound (derived from semantics.json and schema_graph.json with source hashes recorded), but the three API paths are not. A renamed, misspelled or stale entry would survive the gate. The APIs are in fact exercised (crates/scm-sdk/examples/response_defaults.rs:8-21 runs from the extracted archive on both toolchains), so the practical risk is low, but the ledger itself is unverified in a repository where every other ledger resolves to source.
findings.required_fix: In tools/response_defaults.py, derive or verify each rustOnlyAdditions entry against the declaring source (e.g. `pub fn without_response_defaults` and `pub fn response_defaults` in crates/scm-sdk/src/config.rs:406,411 and the `ResponseWithoutDefaults` variant of `pub enum Mode` in crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:26), raising on absence, and add a tools/test_g10_release.py assertion that each recorded path resolves and appears in the packaged example or a named regression test.

findings.description: docs/g10-0.1.1-plan.md:89-95 requires the complete unpublished package delta in the changelog, including example and metadata changes. docs/checks/phase-91-package-delta.json:38-43 records examples/response_defaults.rs as an "added" packaged file, but the 0.1.1 "Added" section (lines 5-15) lists only the two RequestOptions methods and the Mode variant. The new packaged, executable example is a user-visible archive addition that the changelog never mentions; README.md:24 references it, so the omission is inconsistent rather than deliberate.
findings.required_fix: Add a changelog entry for the new packaged offline example examples/response_defaults.rs under 0.1.1 "Added", and confirm the remaining delta rows (.cargo_vcs_info.json, Cargo.toml, Cargo.toml.orig, Cargo.lock, src/engine/tests.rs) are each accounted for by an existing bullet before the release commit.

findings.description: Phase 91 bookkeeping lags the executed gate. milestones.independent_verification is "pending_final_gate" with no evidence array, and scope_evidence.preliminary_tests.status (line 2093) still reads "passed; final source-bound gate remains pending", although docs/checks/phase-91.json records passed=true for the reviewed source 6f0c3cf at 2026-10-18T15:12:37Z with source_unchanged=true. The record understates completed work rather than overstating it, and this file is excluded from source hashing, so correcting it does not invalidate the review — but as written the progress source of truth does not point at the passing receipt.
findings.required_fix: Before advancement, set milestones.independent_verification to passed with evidence ["docs/checks/phase-91.json"] and source_sha256 "6f0c3cfb3690c6b948dbb0544623baf340ecd9205c8d4de67b73175aeb0e02e2", and update scope_evidence.preliminary_tests.status to reference the executed gate instead of describing it as pending.

findings.description: Corpus-level proof of the new mode is JSON-level only. responses_without_defaults_keep_oracle_acceptance_and_omit_only_defaults compares normalized serde_json values, and the 27,216-case typed fixture oracle (tools/generate_models.py --verify-fixtures, docs/checks/phase-91.json:633) runs only under the default response policy. Typed decoding after suppression is proven for Red Team targets (tests/red_team_resources_contracts.rs:2027) and two engine paths, which is what docs/g10-0.1.1-plan.md:36-39 requires, but generated untagged enums elsewhere could in principle select a different variant when a defaulted discriminator-like field is suppressed. No such case was found during review (MultiTurnStatefulConfig/MultiTurnStatelessConfig are not combined into an untagged Rust enum), so this is unmeasured residual scope rather than a known defect.
findings.required_fix: Optional hardening for a follow-up: extend the typed fixture oracle (tools/generate_models.py --verify-fixtures) or add a typed-corpus test that decodes each accepted specimen under Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults and asserts the same Rust variant selection, or record this explicitly as a scoped limitation in docs/VALIDATION.md alongside the existing claim at lines 25-26.

evidence: docs/checks/phase-91.json:3-6 records source_sha256 6f0c3cfb3690c6b948dbb0544623baf340ecd9205c8d4de67b73175aeb0e02e2, source_unchanged true and passed true, matching the reviewed source stated in the prompt.

All 49 recorded checks have exit_code 0 and timeout false (grep over docs/checks/phase-91.json shows 49 exit_code entries, all 0), and the command list matches tools/check_phase.py:82-128 item for item, so no command was silently dropped or substituted.

crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:766-776: the absent property is still walked, the key copy budget is charged via copy_text before the insertion decision, and only `result.insert` is gated on `present.is_some() || self.mode.inserts_defaults()` — the exact phase-90 counterexample.

crates/scm-sdk/tests/schema_contracts.rs:72-78 asserts both policies accept iff max_copied_bytes >= 42 across copied in 26..=70, with the byte arithmetic spelled out in the comment; lines 79-86 compare both policies for max_work and max_nodes in 1..=64.

crates/scm-sdk/tests/schema_contracts.rs:9-42 iterates semantics.json, asserts exactly 23 default bindings, that Request and Response still materialize each original default, that ResponseWithoutDefaults yields None, and that supplied values and explicit nulls are accepted identically by both response policies.

crates/scm-sdk/tests/schema_contracts.rs:252-285 runs every oracle JSON case under ResponseWithoutDefaults, asserts the recorded count equals fixtures counts.jsonCases, asserts accept/reject agreement with the response oracle, asserts omitted > 0 so the corpus genuinely exercises suppression, and only_defaults_differ (lines 224-250) proves no input-present key is ever dropped and no key is invented.
docs/checks/phase-91.json:616 records the independent oracle run: 60271 jsonCases, 12956 accepted, 47315 rejected, unresolvedValidSpecimens empty; line 633 records 27216 typed cases and 0 failures.

crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_resources_contracts.rs:2071-2120 covers get, list, create, update, probe, update_profile and list_all with exact serialized equality against the sent documents (same() at line 144-146); lines 2124-2128 assert Decode rejection with operation red_team.targets.get under both policies; lines 2131-2153 assert the eleven operation names and the skip=0/limit=1 and skip=1/limit=1 page queries.

crates/scm-sdk/src/engine/tests.rs:2461-2502 and 2506-2533 prove the option reaches Gateway SSE contract events and buffered alternative-contract (send_contract_one_of) decoding, each asserting the default policy still inserts basic_auth_location HEADER and the opt-in does not.

crates/scm-sdk/src/config.rs:375-380 sets response_defaults true in the only RequestOptions constructor; engine.rs:474-477 clones caller options so the per-operation choice survives pagination; engine.rs:538 keeps request validation on Mode::Request.

crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:491-544 shows walk() branching only on node kind, never on the new mode, so acceptance and union/one-of selection are mode-independent by construction; parse_one_of_with_limits (lines 165-195) selects on Ok/Err with a shared budget.

docs/checks/phase-91-package-1.89.0.json:778-796 records `cargo +1.89.0 run --example response_defaults --all-features --locked --offline` executed from the extracted archive with exit_code 0; scripts/check-package.py:148-149 appends that command whenever the example is packaged, so both toolchains ran it.

docs/checks/phase-91-package-delta.json enumerates all eleven changed packaged files against published 0.1.0 archive 6d555d95..., and scripts/verify-publication.py:169-175 fails on any path outside the reviewed allowlist or on any removal.

scripts/verify-publication.py:56-102 requires registry owner cdot65, matching version/crate/yanked, checksum equal to both the downloaded archive digest and the clean proof, byte-identical file rows, clean embedded VCS, matching Cargo.toml identity, and MSRV proof equality; tools/test_g10_release.py:130-189 exercises dirty, failed, partial, unexecuted, wrong-owner, wrong-version, wrong-checksum and resigned-dirty-VCS rejections.

docs/checks/phase-08-live-attempt-08.json:1-33 is a sanitized, source-bound receipt (runtimeInputsSha256, binarySha256, commandTemplate with [external-registration] placeholders, crateVersion 0.1.1); tools/live_evidence.py:266 and 276 require runtimeInputsSha256 to equal the current runtime fingerprint and the report version to equal the crate manifest version, and that check passed in the gate.

docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md:13-31 states the limitations without promotion: three 403 Red Team reads, two unexplained 400s with an SDK request-shape defect explicitly not excluded, one uncorrelated scan-ID lookup, and the attempt-07 parser failure preserved in docs/checks/phase-91-live-refresh-attempt-07.json.

docs/checks/phase-91-attempt-01.json, -02.json and -03.json are retained genuine failures (attempt-03 records passed=false with exit_code 1 at line 1124), matching the dispositions in docs/phase-status.json:2200-2219.

contracts/response-defaults.json lists all 23 bindings with distinct source node ids, product ownership, JSON field, default value and Rust types, including shared bindings listed once with every owning schema (for example s000093 with three uses); tools/response_defaults.py:79-80 raises if the denominator changes, and --check compares both the JSON and docs/RESPONSE_DEFAULTS.md byte for byte.

docs/checks/phase-91.json:688 confirms the frozen denominator is unchanged (frozenCapabilities 3820, implemented 3820, unresolved 0); line 722 shows qualification with unexplainedGaps 0 and liveVerified 16 against 448 operations.

tools/test_g10_release.py:43-57 pins canonical hashes of the crate dependencies, features and the locked external package set plus rust-version 1.89, enforcing the plan's "dependencies and feature defaults remain identical to 0.1.0" requirement; docs/checks/phase-91.json:997 shows the fresh advisory scan over 206 packages with freshHead true.

docs/checks/phase-91-private-material.json:3-8 records a real scan at 2026-10-18T14:54:46Z bound to source 6f0c3cf with sourceUnchanged true, 1390 git-visible files, zero selected-value matches and zero new tenant occurrences; the gate's --check re-verified its freshness.

crates/scm-sdk/src/engine/tests.rs:2117-2125 shows the cancellation test still asserts a 1-second timeout and Ok(0) zero-bytes-read, widened only to ConnectionReset, matching docs/g10-0.1.1-plan.md:78-80.

.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:72 runs `python3 tools/check_phase.py --phase 91 --verification-only`, and tools/test_ci.py:82 and :310 were updated from the phase-8 expectations, as docs/g10-0.1.1-plan.md:113-115 requires.

Sampled defaulted fields are all Optional with serde(default) — EvalSummary at generated.rs:33714-33723, ChannelListResponse at 10596-10603, CustomTopicListResponse at 18243-18250, SecurityProfileListResponse at 166198-166205 — so suppressing a default cannot make typed decoding fail.
docs/checks/release-registry-0.1.1.json is absent from the docs/checks directory listing, while README.md:20, docs/STABILITY.md:4 and docs/RELEASE.md:6 all link it.
limitations: Read-only review: I did not execute any command, compile anything, or contact any network service. All pass/fail conclusions about compilers, packages, cross targets, tracing stress and dependency policy rest on the recorded receipts in docs/checks/phase-91*.json, whose internal consistency with tools/check_phase.py I verified but whose execution I could not independently reproduce.

I did not read any credential file, tenant registration, or anything outside this repository, so the live receipt's sanitization is assessed from the committed envelope and the validator in tools/live_evidence.py only; I cannot confirm what the external registration contained.

Publication, tagging and the clean --require-clean package proofs are post-review steps by design (docs/g10-0.1.1-plan.md:135-142), so this review judges only the source and qualification gate. crates.io state, the v0.1.1 tag and remote CI are unverified and must not be read as accepted here.

The 60,271-case oracle corpus and 27,216 typed fixtures were not re-derived; I relied on the recorded schema-oracle and verify-fixtures outputs plus the Rust tests that consume contracts/native-fixtures/schemas.json.

I sampled, rather than exhaustively audited, the 448-method ledger, the generated model corpus and the 3,820-capability export ledger; my conclusions there follow from the passing --check generators, which fail closed on staleness.

Mode-independence of acceptance is argued from reading walk(), object(), parse_one_of_with_limits and the two suppression sites plus the full-corpus differential test. That is strong evidence but not a proof over all schema shapes and all caller-supplied ValidationLimits combinations.
